summary: Verified plan v1 of tier2-webhook (scale: feature, build_mode: design-only, 1 milestone, 5 steps) on all three lenses, round 1 of the two the feature tier allows. Executability passes on 5/5 steps: both named agents resolve, are runtime, non-deprecated and requires_org false, and every declared output is one the named agent's Output Contract produces. Grounding is refuted on M1-S02 and M1-S03 and testability on M1-S04, so the outcome is plan-rejected with three blockers and nine warnings. Every skill, template, decision-tree and agent citation resolves; all ten tree-cited branch quotes match the cited line modulo an ASCII-arrow transliteration; all nine declared checkers exist, accept the flag form declared, exit 1 on a missing directory, and were run on an empty directory to test each step's failure power. The two blockers that need the planner are a field permission the build needs and grants nowhere (Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c under API 67 user mode) and a queue-Id resolution mechanism no cited skill documents; the third is a testability defect on M1-S04's own tests, which amend-step cannot fix at status planned.
confidence_rationale: HIGH per the plan-verifier rubric: all three lenses ran on all five steps plus the milestone and the cross-step set; every verdict carries evidence naming the file read or the command run and what it printed; and no refutation rests on a missing file - each of the three rests on a contradiction between two things that are both on disk. The one judgement call made against the letter of a lens row (the org-only clause of M1-S04's manual test, which the row says to refute at non-ask scales) is recorded as a warning with its reasoning rather than silently dropped.

findings.title: No artefact grants FLS on Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c, which two steps read and write in user mode
findings.detail: Raised by the grounding lens on M1-S02. Tier2_Webhook_Admin's fieldPermissions is scoped to Integration_Failure__c. M1-S03 reads Case.Tier2_Notified_At__c for the ten-minute suppression window and writes it on webhook success; M1-S04 queries it for the 24-hour success check. D14 and Q23 put both in API 67.0 default user mode as the escalating or scheduling user, and AGENT_CONTRACT's version table says user mode enforces FLS on SOQL and DML with no keyword at all. M1-S04's own inputs.running_user names the gap - 'Tier2_Webhook_Admin from M1-S02 carries the Integration_Failure__c half' - and no assumptions[] row covers the other half.

findings.title: M1-S03's escalation detection needs a Queue-to-Group-Id lookup that no cited skill documents
findings.detail: Raised by the grounding lens on M1-S03. The step detects 'OwnerId changed in this save to the Tier_2_Engineering queue', which requires resolving a queue developer name to a Group Id. None of the nine cited skills carries that mechanism and neither does apex-builder's own 33-entry dependencies.skills. skills/apex/apex-hardcoded-id-elimination does, in a worked example that is literally Case routing to a Tier 2 queue, and apex-builder's REFUSAL_SECURITY_GUARD clause (d) refuses the hardcoded-Id alternative - so the step as written leaves the builder a choice between freestyling and a refusal.

findings.title: Every automated test on M1-S04 passes against an empty artefacts directory
findings.detail: Raised by the testability lens on M1-S04, the 'Test can fail' row. Run against an empty directory, check_apex_scheduled_jobs.py and check_apex_queueable_patterns.py both exit 0 with a 'nothing to check' warning, the xml test has nothing to parse, and the manifest test is skipped-not-applicable under the Apex exception. M1-S01 and M1-S02 are caught by the always-on manifest check and M1-S03 by check_callouts_and_http_integrations.py, which exits 1 on an empty tree; M1-S04 has no equivalent. check-outputs still gates set-status built, which is why this is P1 rather than P0, but the row is refuted on its own terms.

findings.title: All ten decision-tree branch quotes are transliterated rather than verbatim
findings.detail: Raised by the grounding lens across the plan. The trees write the branch with a Unicode arrow and column padding; the plan writes '->' with collapsed spacing. Every quote matches its cited line after that normalisation, so no branch is fabricated - but a verifier that takes the row literally would refute all ten tree-cited decisions. Separately: the planner's envelope and the driver's log both say eleven of the fourteen decisions cite a tree branch; the count is ten (D1, D2, D4, D5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D11, D12), with four on a source_reference (D3, D10, D13, D14).

findings.title: Two checkers have no severity flag and fail on advisory findings; the artefacts must clear more than the plan records
findings.detail: check_object_creation_and_design.py returns 1 if any entry lands in all_issues, and its WARN strings go into that same list: a missing <enableSearch> element and a missing or empty <description> fail M1-S01 as surely as deploymentStatus InDevelopment or sharingModel ReadWrite do, and the step's inputs name neither element. check_platform_events_apex.py returns 1 on any finding at any severity, so a REVIEW-severity discarded publish result inside a test class fails M1-S03. Both claims in the plan ('exits 1 on its WARN tier', 'exits 1 on any finding at any severity') are correct as far as they go; the artefact constraints they imply are what the step inputs are missing.
